question: Regarding the monetary operations of the Dutch East India Company in India, which of the following statements is correct?
options: The Dutch were never permitted to mint coins in India and had to rely entirely on Spanish dollars.
The Dutch obtained minting rights from local rulers and minted gold Pagodas at Pulicat, which bore the image of the Hindu deity Venkateshwara.
The Dutch introduced the silver Rupee as the sole currency of the Coromandel coast, replacing gold coins.
The Dutch mint at Surat was the largest gold-producing mint in Mughal India.
explanation: The Dutch obtained minting privileges from the rulers of Vellore (the late Vijayanagara rulers) and later from the Nawab of the Carnatic. They minted the famous gold 'Porto Novo Pagodas' and 'Pulicat Pagodas' showing the image of Lord Venkateshwara (Vishnu). These gold coins were highly valued and accepted across South India and the East Indies.
